frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The wild predatory canid — the wolf as a concrete entity; in its Quranic deployment, the solitary predator whose threat attaches specifically to a human charge left without guard.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The wild predatory canid — the wolf as a concrete entity; in its Quranic deployment, the solitary predator whose threat attaches specifically to a human charge left without guard.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: All three occurrences are the single definite noun al-dhi'b ("the wolf") inside the Yusuf narrative (12:13, 12:14, 12:17). In every occurrence the wolf is the subject of "devour" (akala) with Yusuf as object, and in every occurrence the devouring is non-actual: feared by Yaqub (12:13), hypothesized by the brothers (12:14), and falsely alleged by them (12:17). The wolf never appears on-scene; it exists only within speech about an unwitnessed event. The stable root contribution across all three is the concrete wolf-entity as the paradigmatic danger to the unguarded.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Root residue = the wolf-entity itself (wild predatory canid). Subtracted as non-root layers: (a) FORM — all three are the same bare noun, so form contributes nothing differential; (b) CONSTRUCTION — the "devourer" role comes from the frame [dhi'b as subject of akala + Yusuf as object], not the root; (c) CONTEXT — the feared/hypothetical/alleged (non-actual) status of the devouring comes from reported speech in the Yusuf narrative (qala/qalu in all three verses), and the "unguarded victim" motif comes from 12:13's ghafilun and 12:17's "we left Yusuf with our belongings". After subtraction the residue is non-empty: a specific predator species-entity.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: None exists in the confirmed set. The nearest candidate for tension is 12:17, where the wolf's act is a fabrication — but the fabricated status belongs to the speech-act context, not the root: the lie only works because the wolf-entity is a plausible devourer, which presupposes rather than contradicts the proposed contribution.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: A richer hypothesis: the root contributes not just "wolf" but "the invoked-yet-absent predator / the scapegoat threat that never materializes," since in all 3 occurrences the wolf is talked about but never acts in reality. Rejected as root residue because the non-actuality is fully explained by the reported-speech construction and single-narrative context; attributing it to the root would violate layer separation. It remains a true generalization about Quranic usage, but at the context layer.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct Quran-internally from sab' (al-sabu', 5:3 — generic predator that actually kills livestock) and qaswarah (74:51 — lion, agent of flight/terror): the wolf-root alone is deployed as a named, specific, human-directed threat conditioned on lapsed guardianship, and alone appears only in non-actual (feared/alleged) predation. However, with one lexeme, one syntactic frame, and one narrative cluster, this distinctiveness cannot be triangulated across independent contexts, which caps result strength.
internal_discovery.rationale: Universal presence holds cleanly: 3/3 occurrences carry the identical concrete contribution (the wolf-entity), with zero resistant cases, so PREFERRED is warranted. Strength is WEAK not because of any inconsistency but because the evidence base is minimal for induction: a single nominal lexeme, a single construction (subject of akala), and a single narrative episode provide no cross-context variation against which the proposed contribution could be stress-tested or falsified. The finding is certain as far as it goes, but shallow: the corpus permits identifying the referent and its single deployed role, nothing deeper.

adversarial_verification.notes: Root *Ab = ٱلذِّئْب "the wolf"; 3/3 occurrences are Form-N nouns, ALL inside one Surah Yusuf pericope (12:13, 12:14, 12:17) within a single narrative motif (brothers' wolf-pretext). CORE of the proposed contribution ("wild predatory canid, wolf as concrete entity") is universally present — it is literally the same noun in all three, hence not REFUTED. But the ELABORATION ("solitary predator whose threat attaches specifically to a human charge left without guard") is CONTEXT bleed: the "unguarded charge" idea is supplied by narrative tokens (غافلون in 12:13; تركنا يوسف عند متاعنا in 12:17), not by the root, so it violates the required subtraction of construction/context from root residue. FAILING OCCURRENCE = 12:14: the wolf is invoked precisely inside an assertion of GUARDEDNESS (وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ, "while we are a strong band"), which inverts/contradicts the "left without guard" specification rather than instantiating it — the whole rhetorical point is that Yusuf would NOT be unguarded. Thus the contribution as worded is not demonstrably present at 12:14. DISTINCTIVENESS: the bare "wolf" lexeme is distinct vs nearest roots (كلب etc.), so core distinctiveness holds, but that distinctiveness is just the dictionary lexeme, not an induced residue. FALSIFIABILITY: effectively nil — all occurrences are one noun in one story with no contrasting deployment, so root residue cannot be separated from narrative context and the claim cannot be tested; hence falsifiable=false. Under non-negotiable root unity, the over-specified contribution cannot be SUPPORTED (fails at 12:14); the reducible core "wolf as concrete entity" would hold universally but is not what was proposed.
